agents.description: Scores the completeness of a metadata record against fixed criteria.

json_schema.$comment: Generated from quality.yaml by `uv run dd-gen-schema <path to quality.yaml>`. Do not edit.
json_schema.description: An existing metadata record about a dataset, as a repository or catalogue holds it. The input a quality or validation agent assesses. Slots are the DCAT and Dublin Core terms a minimal record carries; TODO(#22): widen when a real repository export is exercised.

identifier.description: The record's own identifier, e.g. a DOI or a catalogue URI.

licence.description: The licence the record declares, as an IRI or SPDX identifier.

schema_class.description: Type designator: the name of the class this object is an instance of. Discriminates the input and payload unions, and lets a consumer name a payload class it does not recognise.

json_schema.title: MetadataRecord

json_schema.$comment: Generated from quality.yaml by `uv run dd-gen-schema <path to quality.yaml>`. Do not edit.

criterion.description: The quality criterion assessed, e.g. licence_present.

grounded_on.description: The retrieved things this object rests on. For grounding mode retrieval, each entry names a retrieval span; for input_only and none, the single entry is the input itself (source_id input:<invocation_id>, content_hash the dd-input-json-v1 hash).

message.description: The finding, as a sentence a reviewer can act on.

GroundingRef.description: The identity and content hash of one retrieved thing a payload rests on. The only way a payload may name an external resource as a decided identity, and the only place it names it: what the reference identifies is read from the evidence item with the same source_id and content_hash (docs/specs/grounding.md). The linter matches every GroundingRef against a retrieval span on both fields.
GroundingRef.title: GroundingRef

json_schema.description: The payload of a quality or validation agent: a score over an existing record and the findings behind it. Grounded on the input itself (grounding mode input_only or none).

grounded_on.description: The retrieved things this object rests on. For grounding mode retrieval, each entry names a retrieval span; for input_only and none, the single entry is the input itself (source_id input:<invocation_id>, content_hash the dd-input-json-v1 hash).

schema_class.description: Type designator: the name of the class this object is an instance of. Discriminates the input and payload unions, and lets a consumer name a payload class it does not recognise.

summary.description: A short summary of the findings in plain language, for the researcher. It restates the findings and changes none of them.

summary_derivation.description: How the summary came about: template, the rules' own summary, or model, where a model wrote it from the findings.

json_schema.title: QualityReview

agents.title: Metadata Reviewer

agents.description: Recommends controlled vocabularies, ontologies and data formats from FAIRsharing for a dataset profile, whether its data are collected or still being planned, grounded on the registry records it retrieved. Ranking rules choose first; a model may add records it found and note doubts, never remove one. Each recommendation is proposed for the researcher to choose in their project.

json_schema.$comment: Generated from standards.yaml by `uv run dd-gen-schema <path to standards.yaml>`. Do not edit.

CategoryCount.description: One category of a field and how many rows hold it, rounded.
CategoryCount.title: CategoryCount

ConfidenceBand.description: A band of the detector's highest score: low below 0.5, medium from 0.5 and below 0.85, high from 0.85. A low finding is reported, not dropped.
ConfidenceBand.title: ConfidenceBand

DisclosureCheck.description: What the disclosure check of a field's summary values did: the rules, their parameters, the tool and how many values it left out, never which (docs/specs/personal-data.md).

check_rounding_base.description: The base counts were rounded to.

check_rules.description: The rules applied, such as minimum threshold, k-th value range, p-ratio, nk dominance, zeros disclosive and rounding.

check_suppressed.description: How many of the field's summary values were left out. Never which.

check_tool.description: The output checker that applied the rules, such as acro.

DisclosureCheck.title: DisclosureCheck

FactKind.description: What a project fact is about (docs/specs/projects.md).
FactKind.title: FactKind

FieldSummary.description: Summary values of one table field that the inventory command computed where the data live and passed through statistical disclosure control before writing (docs/specs/personal-data.md). A value that failed a rule is absent, never altered to pass; every count is at least the check's threshold and rounded to its base, and a range is never the raw minimum and maximum.

summary_categories.description: The field's categories that at least k rows hold, with their counts. Rarer categories are left out and counted in check_suppressed.

summary_mean.description: The mean of a numeric field's values, missing-value codes left out, written only when the threshold and dominance rules pass.

summary_missing_codes.description: Values the field holds that are often used for missing data (-99, -999, 999, 9999, NA, N/A, NaN, null, .), each held by at least k rows, with their counts.

summary_null_count.description: How many of the rows read hold no value in the field, rounded.

summary_range_high.description: The upper bound of the field's values, the k-th largest, as summary_range_low.

summary_range_low.description: The lower bound of the field's values: the k-th smallest, so that at least k rows (the check's threshold) lie at or below it. A number or an ISO 8601 date or time, as text.

summary_rows_read.description: How many rows were read to compute the summaries, rounded.

FieldSummary.title: FieldSummary

FileDecision.description: Whether a file of the inventory is to be deposited.
FileDecision.title: FileDecision

FileInventory.description: The facts about a dataset's files that the project holds in place of the files (docs/specs/projects.md): for each file its path, size, digest and format, and for a table its fields. Made by a command run where the data live; it never contains a file's content. advisor.files reads it.

inventory_files.description: Every file the command read, sorted by path: under the dataset's root folder, or, in an inventory made of parts, under each part's folder.

inventory_identified_with.description: What identified the formats, such as fido 1.6.1 with PRONOM signatures v109, or that only file extensions were used.

inventory_limitations.description: What the inventory left out or could not do, such as files it skipped.

inventory_parts.description: The scans the inventory is made of, when it is made of more than one folder. Absent, the inventory is one scan of one folder and its paths are relative to that folder. Present, every file's path begins with one part's folder; inventory_made_at is the latest part's, inventory_tool and inventory_tool_version are those of that part, and inventory_limitations holds any that concern no one part, then every part's limitations, each after "In <folder>: ".

inventory_personal_data.description: Where a personal-data detector found possible personal data (docs/specs/personal-data.md). Absent, no detector ran, or the inventory was made by a command without one; empty, a detector ran and found nothing, which does not mean the data hold none. In an inventory made of parts, it is every part's findings, and absent if any part's are absent.

inventory_tool.description: The command that made the inventory, such as dd-inventory.

inventory_tool_version.description: The version of the command that made the inventory.

schema_class.description: Type designator: the name of the class this object is an instance of. Discriminates the input and payload unions, and lets a consumer name a payload class it does not recognise.

FileInventory.title: FileInventory

FileRole.description: What part a file plays in a dataset, as the researcher states it (docs/specs/projects.md).
FileRole.title: FileRole

FindingTarget.description: What part of a file a personal-data finding concerns.
FindingTarget.title: FindingTarget

IdentificationMethod.description: How a file's format was identified, from strongest to weakest (docs/specs/projects.md).
IdentificationMethod.title: IdentificationMethod

InventoryFile.description: One file of a dataset, as the inventory command found it.

file_description.description: What the file is, in the researcher's words. The inventory command never fills it; a researcher states it beside the facts the command found (docs/specs/projects.md).

file_fields.description: For a table, its fields as a Frictionless Table Schema inferred from a sample of rows.

file_identified_by.description: How the PRONOM identifiers were arrived at: by the inventory command, or chosen by the researcher where the command found several matches or none.

file_media_type.description: The file's media type (MIME type), when it could be told.

file_path.description: The file's path relative to the dataset's root folder, with forward slashes; in an inventory made of parts, it begins with its part's folder. Never an absolute path, which would say where the data live.

file_pronom_ids.description: Every PRONOM unique identifier (PUID) the file matched, such as fmt/95 or x-fmt/18. More than one means the identification is ambiguous; none means the format is unknown.

file_role.description: What part the file plays in the dataset, as the researcher states it. Unset means not stated, not data.

file_sha256.description: The SHA-256 digest of the file's bytes, in lowercase hex, by which the file deposited can be shown to be the file described.

InventoryFile.title: InventoryFile

InventoryPart.description: One scan of one folder, mounted at a folder name in an inventory made of several (docs/specs/projects.md). Every file of the inventory lies under exactly one part's folder, and a part is replaced whole when its folder is scanned again.

part_folder.description: The folder name the part is mounted at, such as instrument or raw/2024: relative, with forward slashes, and no empty, . or .. segment. Every file of the part has a path that begins with it and a slash. No part's folder is another's or lies inside another's.

part_identified_with.description: What identified the formats of the part's files, as inventory_identified_with.

part_limitations.description: What the scan of the part's folder left out or could not do.

part_made_at.description: When the part's folder was scanned.

part_personal_data.description: The part's findings, as inventory_personal_data, with paths that begin with the part's folder. Absent, no detector ran on the part.

part_tool.description: The command that scanned the part's folder, such as dd-inventory.

part_tool_version.description: The version of the command that scanned the part's folder.

InventoryPart.title: InventoryPart

LocationPrecision.description: The precision at which a location may be published.
LocationPrecision.title: LocationPrecision

MissingCodeCount.description: A value that a field may use for missing data, such as -99 or NA, and how many rows hold it, rounded.
MissingCodeCount.title: MissingCodeCount

PersonalDataFinding.description: Where the inventory command found what may be personal data, and how sure it is (docs/specs/personal-data.md). It never holds a matched value, any part of one, an offset into a file, a row number or an example: a kind, a place, bands and the detector only. A finding is a prompt for a person, never a decision.

finding_column.description: The table column the finding concerns, for a column or a field name.

finding_confidence.description: How sure the detector is, as a band of its highest score.

finding_detector.description: The detector, its version and its configuration, such as the recognisers that ran, so that a reader knows what was looked for.

finding_examined.description: How much was examined: the sampled, non-empty values of a column, or the characters of a text file. Absent for a name.

finding_file.description: The path of the file the finding concerns, as file_path; or, for a folder's name, the folder's path followed by a slash.

finding_kind.description: What the detector took the data to be.

finding_proportion.description: The share of a column's sampled, non-empty values that matched, as a band so that it cannot be turned back into a count. Present for a column only.

finding_target.description: What part of the file was examined.

PersonalDataFinding.title: PersonalDataFinding

PersonalDataKind.description: What a personal-data finding took the data to be (docs/specs/personal-data.md). The first kinds come from matching values; the last four from matching names against a keyword table, by category.
PersonalDataKind.title: PersonalDataKind

ProjectFact.description: One fact about a project that a check agent proposes and a person confirms: a funder, a repository a funder or institution requires, whether a file is deposited, whether a sensitive field or file may be published and at what precision, the licence, an output a data management plan committed to share, a standard, vocabulary or format the researcher chose for the dataset, which attached document is the project's data management plan, or what data the project collects and how, or what the project is for, its field of study and when it runs (docs/specs/projects.md). fact_kind says which of the value slots apply; fact_subject is the key a person's decision counts by, so the last decision on a subject stands. An agent's payload carries proposals in proposed_facts; only a person's decision makes one a fact, and the conductor gives the facts a person decided to every drafter and orchestrator in the project as project_decisions, without proposed_because.

commitment_access.description: For a sharing commitment, how openly the plan committed to share the output (such as open, embargoed or on request), as the plan says it; absent where it says nothing.

commitment_document.description: For a sharing commitment, the digest of the attached document's text (its documentation_digest) the quote is from.

commitment_licence.description: For a sharing commitment, the licence the plan committed to, as the plan names it; absent where it names none.

commitment_quote.description: For a sharing commitment, the plan's own words the commitment was read from, verbatim, so the person deciding can see the passage it rests on.

commitment_repository.description: For a sharing commitment, the repository the plan committed to share the output in, as the plan names it; absent where it names none. A plan that names several for one output gives a sharing commitment for each.

data_collected.description: For a data description fact, what data the project collects, produces or reuses, and of which types, in the researcher's words.

data_collection_method.description: For a data description fact, how the data are collected or produced, in the researcher's words.

data_formats.description: For a data description fact, the file formats the data are kept in, in the researcher's words.

data_reused.description: For a data description fact, which existing data the project reuses, and how, in the researcher's words.

data_volume.description: For a data description fact, how much data the project expects, in the researcher's words.

fact_check_kind.description: The kind of check that raised the fact, in the checking agent's words, such as duplicate, system_file or third_party. Kept as it was given; the core does not enumerate it.

fact_crossref_funder_id.description: The funder's Crossref Funder ID, as a DOI URL, where it is known.

fact_file_path.description: The path of the file the fact is about, relative to the dataset's root folder, as the inventory gives it.

fact_funder_name.description: The funder's name, as its policy record or the researcher gives it.

fact_funder_ror.description: The funder's ROR identifier, as a URL, where it is known.

fact_kind.description: What the fact is about, which says which value slots apply.

fact_re3data_id.description: The required repository's re3data identifier, such as r3d100010199, where known.

fact_required_by.description: The funders, journals or institutions that require the repository.

fact_subject.description: The key a decision counts by within its kind: the funder's identifier or name, the repository's re3data identifier or name, the file's path, the field or path judged sensitive, licence, or the standard chosen and what it is chosen for. The last decision on a kind and subject stands.

field_name.description: For a field of study fact, the project's field, as the researcher names it or a subject classification gives it.

file_decision.description: Whether the file is to be deposited.

licence_id.description: The licence decided, as an SPDX identifier or a URL.

location_precision.description: For a location that may be published or generalised, the precision agreed. Absent where the subject is not a location.

period_end.description: For a project period fact, when the project ends, as a year, a month or a day; absent where it is not known.

period_start.description: For a project period fact, when the project starts, as a year, a month or a day.

plan_document.description: For a data management plan fact, the digest of the attached document's text (its documentation_digest) that is the project's plan.

proposed_because.description: Why the agent proposes the fact, in a sentence for the person deciding. Kept with the proposal and shown to the person, never given to an agent.

sensitive_subject.description: The field name, or the file path, judged sensitive, such as a lat or lon field, or a file of site coordinates.

sensitivity_decision.description: Whether the sensitive field or file may be published, and how.

standard_id.description: For a standard fact, a persistent identifier of the standard, as a URL, such as its FAIRsharing DOI, where it is known.

standard_kind.description: For a standard fact, what kind of standard was chosen, where it is known.

standard_name.description: For a standard fact, the name of the standard, vocabulary, ontology or format chosen, as its registry record or the researcher gives it.

standard_target.description: For a standard fact, what the standard is chosen for: dataset, or field:<name> for one field of the dataset's tables. Absent means the dataset.

summary_text.description: For a project summary fact, what the project is for, in a few sentences: its aims and the questions it asks.

ProjectFact.title: ProjectFact

ProportionBand.title: ProportionBand

TableField.description: One field of a tabular resource, mirroring a Frictionless Table Schema field descriptor. Frictionless publishes no RDF namespace, so these slots carry see_also rather than a slot_uri (TODO(#20): revisit if Frictionless publishes term IRIs).

field_disclosure_check.description: The disclosure check the field's summary values passed. Present whenever field_summary is.

field_summary.description: The field's summary values (docs/specs/personal-data.md). Absent, no summaries were made: by an older command, in a runtime where they do not run, or with them turned off.

field_type.description: Frictionless field type (string, number, integer, boolean, date, datetime, time, duration, geopoint, ...).

TableField.title: TableField

json_schema.description: A minimal description of a dataset being planned or prepared: what it is about and how it is shaped. Every slot maps onto an external vocabulary rather than a Data Director namespace. In a project the conductor also gives the facts people decided; a decided field of study, description of the data or summary of the project fills what the profile leaves empty (#1529). It also gives the project's inventory; its media types and tables' fields fill what the profile leaves empty (#1540).

project_decisions.description: The facts a person in the project decided (ProjectFact), the last decision on each subject, filled by the conductor and never by the caller. Absent when the run is in no project, or nobody in its project decided any. A drafter treats each as supplied.

project_file_inventory.description: The project's file inventory, as the researcher added it last. In a project the conductor fills it and a caller leaves it out. Absent while the project holds no inventory.

schema_class.description: Type designator: the name of the class this object is an instance of. Discriminates the input and payload unions, and lets a consumer name a payload class it does not recognise.

themes.description: Discipline or subject, as free text or an IRI.

json_schema.title: DatasetProfile

organisation_identifier.description: The organisation's identifier, where ORCID gives one: a URL for ROR, else as given.

organisation_identifier_scheme.description: The scheme of organisation_identifier, in ORCID's words, such as ROR, GRID or RINGGOLD. Present exactly when organisation_identifier is.

put_code.description: ORCID's identifier for the item within the record, by which a researcher chose to keep it.

Affiliation.title: Affiliation

AffiliationKind.description: The kinds of affiliation an ORCID record holds.
AffiliationKind.title: AffiliationKind

ChosenRepository.description: The repository a researcher chose to deposit the project's data in, from the shortlist, by the identifier of the registry that lists it: the conductor fills it into a Message, and into the input of an agent that mixes in GivenProjectRepository, so that the agent knows a repository is chosen and which (docs/specs/projects.md). The last choice stands until a researcher chooses again.

chosen_re3data_id.description: The chosen repository's re3data identifier, such as r3d100010468, where it has one.

chosen_repository_id.description: The chosen repository's identifier: its re3data identifier, such as r3d100010468, where re3data lists it, else its DataCite repository identifier, such as bl.york. The conductor always gives it; a caller that sends only chosen_re3data_id has it given from that.

chosen_repository_name.description: The chosen repository's name, as the pinned re3data export gives it.

ChosenRepository.title: ChosenRepository

ConversationTurn.description: One earlier turn of a conversation, as the caller presents it to the agent. An agent turn names the agent and version that produced it and the invocation it came from.

turn_agent_id.description: For an agent turn, the agent that produced it.

turn_agent_version.description: For an agent turn, the version of the agent that produced it.

turn_invocation_id.description: For an agent turn, the invocation it came from.

turn_text.description: What was said in the turn.

ConversationTurn.title: ConversationTurn

DocumentKind.description: What a project document is for (docs/specs/projects.md).
DocumentKind.title: DocumentKind

DocumentationSummary.description: What one document a researcher attached to a project is, without its text: the conductor fills one per document into a Message so that the agent knows the project holds it (docs/specs/projects.md).

documentation_added_at.description: When the document was added to the project.

documentation_digest.description: The SHA-256 of the document's UTF-8 text, by which the project keeps it.

documentation_is_plan.description: True for the one document a person decided is the project's data management plan (a data_management_plan fact); absent for every other. Only the conductor fills it, from the project's decisions (docs/specs/projects.md).

documentation_media_type.description: The document's media type, text/plain or text/markdown.

documentation_name.description: The file name the researcher attached the document under, without any folder.

documentation_size.description: The size of the document's UTF-8 text, in bytes.

documentation_source_media_type.description: The media type of the Word document or PDF the document's text was read from, inside the deployment; absent for a document attached as text. The project keeps the file beside the text.

DocumentationSummary.title: DocumentationSummary

DraftSummary.description: The latest version of one document drafted in a project, without its text: the conductor fills one per document into a Message so that the agent knows which version is current and whether it was drafted from the inventory the project holds now, rather than relying on what it said of an earlier version (docs/specs/projects.md).

drafted_since_inventory.description: Whether the version was drafted after the project's inventory was last added or revised, so that it reflects which files the inventory now lists. Absent when the project holds no inventory.

version.description: The number of a version within its document, counted from 1.

version_state.description: Whether a person has approved or rejected the version, or not yet decided.

DraftSummary.title: DraftSummary

ExternalIdentifier.description: An identifier from another scheme, as an ORCID record gives it: for a researcher, such as a Scopus Author ID; for a work, such as a DOI.

identifier_type.description: The scheme, in ORCID's words, such as doi or Scopus Author ID.

identifier_url.description: The identifier as a URL, where the record gives one.

ExternalIdentifier.title: ExternalIdentifier

FactKind.description: What a project fact is about (docs/specs/projects.md).
FactKind.title: FactKind

FileDecision.description: Whether a file of the inventory is to be deposited.
FileDecision.title: FileDecision

IntakeAnswer.description: The researcher's current answer to one of the intake's setup questions beside the entry question (dd_sdk.intake), as the project log shows it, with the labels of the options chosen (docs/specs/orchestration.md, invariant 20).

intake_answer_labels.description: The labels of the options the researcher chose, such as "Not sure"; never empty.

intake_question_prompt.description: The intake question as the researcher was asked it.

IntakeAnswer.title: IntakeAnswer

InventoryFormat.description: The files of one media type in a project's inventory, without their paths: the conductor fills one per media type into an InventorySummary, so that the agent knows what kinds of files the dataset holds without asking (docs/specs/projects.md, #1287).

format_file_count.description: How many of the inventory's files are in the group.

format_media_type.description: The media type (MIME type) of the group's files. Absent, the group is of the files whose media type could not be told.

format_pronom_ids.description: Every PRONOM unique identifier (PUID) the group's files matched, sorted.

InventoryFormat.title: InventoryFormat

InventorySummary.description: What the inventory a project holds is, without its files: the conductor fills it into a Message so that the agent knows the project has one (docs/specs/projects.md).

inventory_added_at.description: When the inventory was added to the project, as its latest; a revision, such as files left out in Edit inventory, is added anew.

inventory_digest.description: The inventory's dd-input-json-v1 hash, by which the project keeps it.

inventory_file_count.description: How many files the inventory lists.

inventory_formats.description: The inventory's files grouped by media type, the group with the most bytes first, as the app's inventory view groups them. Absent, the summary was made without them.

inventory_limitations.description: What the inventory left out or could not do, such as files it skipped.

inventory_revised_from_file_count.description: How many files the inventory it replaced listed. Absent when it is the first the project holds.

inventory_table_count.description: How many of the inventory's files are tables whose fields it lists.

inventory_tool.description: The command that made the inventory, such as dd-inventory.

inventory_tool_version.description: The version of the command that made the inventory.

InventorySummary.title: InventorySummary

LocationPrecision.description: The precision at which a location may be published.
LocationPrecision.title: LocationPrecision

ProjectFact.description: One fact about a project that a check agent proposes and a person confirms: a funder, a repository a funder or institution requires, whether a file is deposited, whether a sensitive field or file may be published and at what precision, the licence, an output a data management plan committed to share, a standard, vocabulary or format the researcher chose for the dataset, which attached document is the project's data management plan, or what data the project collects and how, or what the project is for, its field of study and when it runs (docs/specs/projects.md). fact_kind says which of the value slots apply; fact_subject is the key a person's decision counts by, so the last decision on a subject stands. An agent's payload carries proposals in proposed_facts; only a person's decision makes one a fact, and the conductor gives the facts a person decided to every drafter and orchestrator in the project as project_decisions, without proposed_because.

commitment_access.description: For a sharing commitment, how openly the plan committed to share the output (such as open, embargoed or on request), as the plan says it; absent where it says nothing.

commitment_document.description: For a sharing commitment, the digest of the attached document's text (its documentation_digest) the quote is from.

commitment_licence.description: For a sharing commitment, the licence the plan committed to, as the plan names it; absent where it names none.

commitment_quote.description: For a sharing commitment, the plan's own words the commitment was read from, verbatim, so the person deciding can see the passage it rests on.

commitment_repository.description: For a sharing commitment, the repository the plan committed to share the output in, as the plan names it; absent where it names none. A plan that names several for one output gives a sharing commitment for each.

data_collected.description: For a data description fact, what data the project collects, produces or reuses, and of which types, in the researcher's words.

data_collection_method.description: For a data description fact, how the data are collected or produced, in the researcher's words.

data_formats.description: For a data description fact, the file formats the data are kept in, in the researcher's words.

data_reused.description: For a data description fact, which existing data the project reuses, and how, in the researcher's words.

data_volume.description: For a data description fact, how much data the project expects, in the researcher's words.

fact_check_kind.description: The kind of check that raised the fact, in the checking agent's words, such as duplicate, system_file or third_party. Kept as it was given; the core does not enumerate it.

fact_crossref_funder_id.description: The funder's Crossref Funder ID, as a DOI URL, where it is known.

fact_file_path.description: The path of the file the fact is about, relative to the dataset's root folder, as the inventory gives it.

fact_funder_name.description: The funder's name, as its policy record or the researcher gives it.

fact_funder_ror.description: The funder's ROR identifier, as a URL, where it is known.

fact_kind.description: What the fact is about, which says which value slots apply.

fact_re3data_id.description: The required repository's re3data identifier, such as r3d100010199, where known.

fact_required_by.description: The funders, journals or institutions that require the repository.

fact_subject.description: The key a decision counts by within its kind: the funder's identifier or name, the repository's re3data identifier or name, the file's path, the field or path judged sensitive, licence, or the standard chosen and what it is chosen for. The last decision on a kind and subject stands.

field_name.description: For a field of study fact, the project's field, as the researcher names it or a subject classification gives it.

file_decision.description: Whether the file is to be deposited.

licence_id.description: The licence decided, as an SPDX identifier or a URL.

location_precision.description: For a location that may be published or generalised, the precision agreed. Absent where the subject is not a location.

period_end.description: For a project period fact, when the project ends, as a year, a month or a day; absent where it is not known.

period_start.description: For a project period fact, when the project starts, as a year, a month or a day.

plan_document.description: For a data management plan fact, the digest of the attached document's text (its documentation_digest) that is the project's plan.

proposed_because.description: Why the agent proposes the fact, in a sentence for the person deciding. Kept with the proposal and shown to the person, never given to an agent.

sensitive_subject.description: The field name, or the file path, judged sensitive, such as a lat or lon field, or a file of site coordinates.

sensitivity_decision.description: Whether the sensitive field or file may be published, and how.

standard_id.description: For a standard fact, a persistent identifier of the standard, as a URL, such as its FAIRsharing DOI, where it is known.

standard_kind.description: For a standard fact, what kind of standard was chosen, where it is known.

standard_name.description: For a standard fact, the name of the standard, vocabulary, ontology or format chosen, as its registry record or the researcher gives it.

standard_target.description: For a standard fact, what the standard is chosen for: dataset, or field:<name> for one field of the dataset's tables. Absent means the dataset.

summary_text.description: For a project summary fact, what the project is for, in a few sentences: its aims and the questions it asks.

ProjectFact.title: ProjectFact

QuestionAnswer.description: The researcher's answer to one question of a reply, named by its question_key: the values of the options chosen, for a choice question, and the answer in their own words, for a text question or where a choice question allows it.

answer_values.description: The values of the options chosen, for a choice question; empty when the researcher answered in their own words, and always empty for a text question.

answer_words.description: The researcher's answer in their own words: the whole answer to a text question, or an answer given in place of an option where a choice question allows it.

answered_key.description: The question_key of the question answered.

QuestionAnswer.title: QuestionAnswer

ReplyAnswers.description: The researcher's answers to the questions the turn before asked, given together: one QuestionAnswer for each question answered, none for a question skipped. The app checks them against those questions before it sends the turn (docs/specs/orchestration.md).

answer_to.description: The invocation whose reply asked the questions.

given_answers.description: One answer for each question answered, in the order asked; at least one.

ReplyAnswers.title: ReplyAnswers

ResearcherFunding.description: One grant or award on an ORCID record, with its funder.

award_identifier.description: The grant number or award identifier, where the record gives one.

end_year.description: The year it ended; absent while it continues.

funder_identifier.description: The funder's identifier, where ORCID gives one, such as a Crossref Funder ID.

funder_identifier_scheme.description: The scheme of funder_identifier, in ORCID's words, such as FUNDREF or ROR. Present exactly when funder_identifier is.

funding_type.description: The kind of funding, in ORCID's words, such as grant or award.

put_code.description: ORCID's identifier for the item within the record, by which a researcher chose to keep it.

ResearcherFunding.title: ResearcherFunding

ResearcherLink.description: A web page the researcher lists on their ORCID record, such as a personal page.

link_title.description: The name the researcher gave the page.

ResearcherLink.title: ResearcherLink

ResearcherRecord.description: What one researcher in a project chose to keep from their public ORCID record: only the sections and items they ticked, in ORCID's own words, never edited by a person or a model. The conductor fills the project's records into a Message and a DraftRequest so that an agent can draft creators, affiliations, subjects and funding from them (docs/specs/projects.md). Email addresses are never kept, even public ones.

affiliations.description: The researcher's affiliations they kept, the current ones first.

biography.description: The researcher's biography, as their ORCID record gives it.

country.description: A country the researcher's ORCID record names, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.

external_identifiers.description: The researcher's identifiers in other schemes, as their ORCID record lists them.

fundings.description: The researcher's grants and awards they kept, the current ones first.

keywords.description: The researcher's own keywords for their research, as their ORCID record lists them.

orcid_id.description: The researcher's ORCID iD, as its URL, such as https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1825-0097.

other_names.description: Other names the researcher is known by, as their ORCID record lists them.

record_retrieved_at.description: When the record was read from ORCID's public API.

record_source.description: The public API address the record was read from.

researcher_links.description: The web pages the researcher's ORCID record lists.

researcher_name.description: The researcher's name as their ORCID record gives it: the credit name, else the given and family names. Absent when they keep their name private or did not keep it.

works.description: The researcher's works they kept, the most recent first: at most 50 are offered, so that an agent's input stays bounded.

works_omitted.description: How many works the record held beyond the 50 offered. Absent when none were left out.

ResearcherRecord.title: ResearcherRecord

ResearcherWork.description: One work on an ORCID record, such as a journal article or a dataset.

journal_title.description: Where the work was published, such as a journal's name.

publication_year.description: The year the work was published.

put_code.description: ORCID's identifier for the item within the record, by which a researcher chose to keep it.

work_identifiers.description: The work's identifiers, such as its DOI.

work_type.description: The work's type, in ORCID's words, such as journal-article or data-set.

ResearcherWork.title: ResearcherWork

SensitivityDecision.description: Whether a sensitive field or file may be published.
SensitivityDecision.title: SensitivityDecision

StandardKind.description: What kind of standard a standard fact names.
StandardKind.title: StandardKind

StepProgress.description: How far one step of the Blueprint's process flow has gone, as the project log shows it: started, done or skipped. A step the list leaves out is open (docs/specs/orchestration.md).
StepProgress.title: StepProgress

StepState.description: How far a process-flow step has gone; a step with none of these states is open.
StepState.title: StepState

TurnRole.description: Who spoke in a conversation turn.
TurnRole.title: TurnRole

VersionState.description: The state of one version of a project document (ADR-0035 decision 6). Every version begins proposed; once approved or rejected, it does not change.
VersionState.title: VersionState

json_schema.description: One conversational turn addressed to an agent: the text of the turn and the conversation so far. The history is part of the input, so the input hash covers everything the agent saw. In a project that holds an inventory, the conductor adds what it is (docs/specs/projects.md); in any project, it adds the entry point chosen, the progress the project log shows and the project's title, if it has one (docs/specs/orchestration.md). It adds the researcher facts people in the project chose to keep from their public ORCID records, the facts they decided, the repository they chose and the latest version of each document drafted in it (docs/specs/projects.md).

history.description: The earlier turns of the conversation, oldest first.

message_text.description: What the user said in this turn.

project_decisions.description: The facts a person in the project decided (ProjectFact), the last decision on each subject, filled by the conductor and never by the caller. Absent when the run is in no project, or nobody in its project decided any. A drafter treats each as supplied.

project_documentation.description: The documents the conversation's project holds, without their text, filled by the conductor and never by the caller. Absent when the run is in no project, or its project holds none.

project_drafts.description: The latest version of each document drafted in the conversation's project, without its text, in the order first drafted, filled by the conductor and never by the caller. Absent when the run is in no project, or its project holds no drafted document.

project_entry.description: The Blueprint entry point (1, 2 or 3) the researcher chose for the conversation's project, the latest chosen. Filled by the conductor and never by the caller; absent when the run is in no project, or none was chosen.

project_entry_by_researcher.description: Whether the researcher chose the project's entry point, so that a model's would be refused; false when an orchestrator's model recorded it. Filled by the conductor and never by the caller; absent when the run is in no project, or no entry point was recorded.

project_intake.description: The researcher's current answers to the intake's setup questions beside the entry question, in the order they are asked, only for a question asked from the project's entry point, filled by the conductor and never by the caller. Absent when the run is in no project, or no such question has been answered. The entry question's answer is `project_entry`.

project_inventory.description: The inventory the conversation's project holds, filled by the conductor and never by the caller. Absent when the run is in no project, or its project holds no inventory.

project_progress.description: The process-flow steps the conversation's project log shows started, done or skipped, in flow order. Filled by the conductor and never by the caller; absent when the run is in no project. Derived from the log on every turn, never stored.

project_repository.description: The repository a researcher in the project chose last, filled by the conductor and never by the caller. Absent when the run is in no project, or nobody in its project has chosen one.

project_researchers.description: The researcher facts the conversation's project holds, one record for each person who kept some, filled by the conductor and never by the caller. Absent when the run is in no project, or nobody in its project kept any.

project_title.description: The conversation's project's latest title. Filled by the conductor and never by the caller; absent when the run is in no project, or the project has no title yet.

project_title_by_researcher.description: Whether a person gave the project its title, so that a model's would be refused; false while the project has no title. Filled by the conductor and never by the caller; absent when the run is in no project.

reply_answers.description: The researcher's answers to the questions the previous turn asked, when they answered them in the form. message_text still carries the answers as prose.

schema_class.description: Type designator: the name of the class this object is an instance of. Discriminates the input and payload unions, and lets a consumer name a payload class it does not recognise.

json_schema.title: Message
